clue.text: A record I included in stuff for trip

indicators.note: the letter I is put within the record's two letters

parts.note: CD, a compact disc, is a record

explanation.surface: Someone files a record among their travel gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trip' suggests a journey, but it is the drug sense: a hallucinogenic experience.
explanation.definitionFit: LSD, the drug that produces a hallucinogenic trip, is known in slang by this name.

clue.text: Shout in line put in further down

indicators.note: the line's letter is placed inside the word for further down

parts.note: below means further down

explanation.surface: An instruction to add a line lower down on a page, read as a shout.
explanation.walkthrough: Saul Bellow, Nobel literature laureate, is one of the writers 11 across joins.
explanation.definitionFit: To roar or yell loudly is a synonym for shouting.

clue.text: Work composed in person, wherein sentences aren't rigidly controlled

parts.note: OP, short for opus, is a work

indicators.note: composed means put together anew, so the letters of 'in person' are rearranged

explanation.surface: A work written in person, and a place where sentences are loosely policed, like grammar left free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sentences' looks grammatical, but these are prison terms.
explanation.definitionFit: A low-security jail lets inmates serving terms move about with few restrictions.

clue.text: One writer after 11, another before 27

definitions.meaning: his surname follows the name at 11 across
His first name precedes the surname at 27 down

explanation.surface: A puzzle about writers' names placed around other entries in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the Welsh poet and the German novelist share this name, once as surname and once as forename.

clue.text: Artist tucked into cheap fish

indicators.note: the artist's letters are placed inside the word for cheap

parts.note: stingy means mean or cheap
RA, a Royal Academician, is an artist

explanation.surface: A painter is sat down to a meal of bargain fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat ray with a venomous tail spine is a kind of fish.

clue.text: Band, live, including old instrument for blowing in the wind

definitions.text: instrument for blowing in the wind

parts.note: a ring, O-shaped, is a band

indicators.note: the word for live holds the letter for old inside it

parts.note: to be is to live

explanation.surface: A band playing live with an old instrument in the open air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blowin' in the Wind' is a Bob Dylan song, the theme here.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodwind is played by blowing into it, and this double-reed one is a member of the woodwind family.

clue.text: Writer is brought into rock band to make music

parts.note: ME, the setter writing the clue

indicators.note: the word 'is' is put inside the band of rock

parts.note: a lode is a vein or band of ore in rock

explanation.surface: An author joins a rock band in order to make music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rock band' suggests a group of musicians; here it is a geological seam.
explanation.definitionFit: To set words to tunes or produce tunes is to make music.

clue.text: Mixed-up confusion of aide's plan

indicators.note: a mixed-up confusion jumbles the letters of 'aide'

explanation.surface: An assistant's scheme is a muddle.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan and a notion or scheme in the mind are synonyms.

clue.text: Abusive remark getting clubs plenty excited

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
heaps means plenty
hot means excited or aroused

explanation.surface: Golf clubs got someone so worked up they said something nasty.
explanation.definitionFit: An unfair or spiteful jibe is idiomatically called this.

clue.text: Money raised orally

indicators.note: orally means the word is heard, spoken aloud

parts.note: bred means raised, as children or animals

explanation.surface: Cash collected by spoken appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' looks like fundraising; it is the sense brought up.
explanation.definitionFit: In slang, cash is called by the name of the staple loaf.

clue.text: 24 across player, joining 2, 16, 22 down and 27

parts.note: Bob, mouth-organ player, who in 2016 won the Nobel Prize in Literature, joining Bellow, Grass, Anatole France and Mann as laureates

explanation.surface: A musician joining a list of other entries in the grid.
explanation.walkthrough: Saul Bellow, Günter Grass, Anatole France and Thomas Mann all won the Nobel Prize in Literature.
explanation.definitionFit: Bob, the songwriter who plays mouth organ, won the Nobel literature prize like those writers.

clue.text: Mention as altered state 11 was in initially

indicators.note: altered means changed, so the letters of 'Mention as' are rearranged

explanation.surface: Say which state the singer first lived in, rearranged.
explanation.walkthrough: Bob Dylan was born in Duluth, in this US state.
explanation.definitionFit: The singer's birthplace, Duluth, is in this Midwestern US state.

clue.text: How too many people have died — sad words finally taken to heart

parts.words: How too many people have died
parts.note: in war is how far too many have perished

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letters of 'sad' and 'words'

explanation.surface: A grim reflection on war deaths, with mournful words absorbed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something taken to heart is directed towards the inner self.

clue.text: Times changing articles

indicators.note: changing means the letters of 'Times' are rearranged

explanation.surface: The newspaper altering its pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articles' suggests newspaper pieces in The Times; it means things.
explanation.definitionFit: Articles in the sense of individual objects or things are synonyms.

clue.text: Member of rock group, like one of which 11 performed

definitions.meaning: one of the band whose members include Jagger and Richards
'Like a ___' is Dylan's famous 1965 song: the answer fills that title

explanation.surface: A rock musician, compared to a song the singer once performed.
explanation.definitionFit: Jagger's band members are each one of these, and Dylan sang 'Like a Rolling Stone'.

clue.text: Management has numbers of Germans reportedly on board?

indicators.note: reportedly means the word is as heard, a sound-alike

parts.note: Lieder are German art songs, numbers in a recital
a ship is what you are on when on board

explanation.surface: A company's management has many German staff, apparently, sitting on the board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'numbers' looks like headcount; it means songs, Schubert-style Lieder.
explanation.definitionFit: Management and direction of an organisation are synonyms, both meaning the guiding role.

clue.text: Collaborator with the law, possibly bent

definitions.meaning: British slang for a police informer
bent is a kind of meadow plant, so possibly an example of the green stuff

explanation.surface: A police informant who may be corrupt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bent' suggests a crooked cop; it is bent, a type of lawn plant. Günter Grass is another Nobel laureate.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang an informer is a nark; bent is a genus of lawn turf.

clue.text: Issues in changing times

indicators.note: changing means the letters of 'times' are rearranged

explanation.surface: Echoes Dylan's 'The Times They Are a-Changin'': problems arise as times change.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue something, such as light or sound, is to give it out.

clue.text: Middle part of winter I originally selected

indicators.note: part of says the letters are found inside the words 'winter I originally'

explanation.surface: Mid-winter as first chosen.
explanation.definitionFit: The inner part of something is its middle.

clue.text: Withdrawn from famous Swedish ceremony, ultimately

indicators.note: ultimately picks the final letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: Someone absent from a celebrated Swedish ceremony: Dylan skipped his Nobel prize-giving.
explanation.definitionFit: A reserved, retiring person is withdrawn, timid in company.

clue.text: Place for minister it's scary to switch

indicators.note: to switch means the letters of 'it's scary' are swapped around

explanation.surface: A clergyman finds changing posts frightening.
explanation.definitionFit: A vestry, the room where a church minister robes, is a synonym.

clue.text: Backed a time and place for big event

indicators.note: backed means written backwards

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, a
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone supported a date and venue for a major occasion.
explanation.definitionFit: A stadium or venue for large gatherings or performances fits the description.

clue.text: Awful act, a sin that's diabolical

indicators.note: awful signals the letters of 'act a sin' are badly mangled

explanation.surface: A terrible deed, a devilish sin.
explanation.definitionFit: Of the devil, diabolical and devilish are synonyms.

clue.text: Energy put into hit since holidays

indicators.note: the energy letter is put inside the word for hit

parts.note: to fist is to hit with a fist
E is the physics symbol for energy
as can mean since, because

explanation.surface: Energy given to a hit since the holidays.
explanation.definitionFit: Festivals or feast days, as in Spain, are holidays.

clue.text: State of departments dictator cut, note

indicators.note: cut means the last letter is chopped off

parts.note: General Franco was Spain's dictator
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A state run in departments where a dictator cut a note.
explanation.walkthrough: Anatole France is another Nobel literature laureate.
explanation.definitionFit: The country is divided administratively into départements, so it is a state of them.

clue.text: High point of rock, clear and passionate

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill top on a moor
to rid is to clear

explanation.surface: Clear summit, passionate climber.
explanation.definitionFit: Torrid, describing an intense love affair, is a synonym of ardent and passionate.

clue.text: Saintly female on instrument, not piano — much smaller one

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed next after
not means the piano letter is left out

parts.note: a harp is a stringed instrument
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
St Monica, mother of St Augustine

explanation.surface: A saint playing an instrument, leaving out the piano for something much smaller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' refers back to instrument: a much smaller instrument than a harp or piano.
explanation.definitionFit: A mouth organ is a tiny instrument compared with a harp, Dylan's trademark.

clue.text: Crowd entertainer

explanation.definitionFit: A multitude is a crowd, and a person receiving guests entertains them.

clue.text: Eg sound of a thunder heard in moment

definitions.text: Eg sound of a thunder heard

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the word 'moment'

explanation.surface: A clap of thunder heard in a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: Thunder was long taken as a portent, so hearing it is an example of a sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Thunder heard was traditionally a portent or warning sign.

clue.text: Play guitar in odd way? Just the opposite

parts.note: ST, street, is a way
rum means odd

explanation.surface: Playing a guitar unusually.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, 'in odd way' puts the way inside the odd word; the question 'Just the opposite' tells you to swap which piece goes inside, so the odd word sits in the way.
explanation.definitionFit: To sweep the fingers across guitar strings is to play it.

clue.text: Part of literary award, we hear, for novelist

indicators.note: we hear means a sound-alike

parts.note: the Man Booker Prize, man being its first part

explanation.surface: A writer hears part of a prize name.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Mann, the German novelist, is another Nobel laureate.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas, the German author of Buddenbrooks, was a novelist.

clue.text: See 14
Diplomacy I preserve, hiding one master of war?

parts.note: tact is diplomacy

indicators.note: hiding means the preserve holds the one inside

parts.note: to can is to preserve food
I is one, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A diplomat hiding something, perhaps a master of strategy.
explanation.walkthrough: Dylan's song 'Masters of War' lies behind the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A strategist skilled in planning battles is a master of warfare.
